subject.title: Bug: Orphaned TaskFlows in `waiting` status permanently block agent heartbeats (requests-in-flight deadlock)

question: What should OpenClaw's default recovery policy be for managed TaskFlows stuck in `waiting` status?
rationale: Current code can detect stale waits, but automatically terminalizing them changes plugin-visible TaskFlow semantics and may break valid external waits unless maintainers choose the contract.

options.title: Operator-controlled recovery
options.body: Keep stale wait detection as a diagnostic and add a clear Doctor/tasks fix path that explicitly marks selected stale waits lost or cancelled.

options.title: Automatic stale-wait expiry
options.body: Make maintenance or gateway startup mark old `waiting` flows lost after a documented timeout, with tests proving legitimate waits are not broken.

options.title: Controller-declared deadlines
options.body: Extend managed TaskFlow metadata so plugin controllers declare timeout/abandonment policy and core only expires flows with that contract.

recommendation.title: Operator-controlled recovery
recommendation.body: Keep stale wait detection as a diagnostic and add a clear Doctor/tasks fix path that explicitly marks selected stale waits lost or cancelled.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest recent owner for the TaskFlow maintenance/audit surface where the policy would be implemented.
